item.title: Craft Log: Machining Custom 301 High-Yield Picks with Brass Ferrules & Manitoba Walnut
item.description:
In the trade, tools are an extension of your nervous system. When you are picking a serrated spool pin in a tight European keyway, your eyes can’t see the shear line; you are relying 100% on tactile friction and microscopic acoustic resonance transmitted up through the pick shank into your fingertips.

Most commercial mass-manufactured picks use cheap stamped steel with dipped rubber or plastic handles that dampen vibration. Over the past month in the wood and metal shop, I set out to produce a set of heirloom-grade tension tools and picks combining 301 High-Yield full-hard stainless steel, solid C360 free-machining brass bolsters, and salvaged Manitoba black walnut scales.

item.title: Bench Restoration: Resurrecting a 1912 Victor Safe 4-Wheel Pack from an Abandoned Prairie Credit Union
item.description:
In the early decades of the twentieth century, every booming railway town across Western Manitoba—from Souris to Minnedosa—had a solid brick bank or credit union anchored by a massive cast-iron safe. Built like battleships to withstand dynamite attacks from wandering train bandits, these safes housed mechanical combination locks that were marvels of Victorian hand-fitted precision.

Last month, during the demolition salvage of an old municipal hall north of Minnedosa, we were tasked with recovering and restoring an authentic 1912 Victor Safe & Lock Co. 4-Wheel Combination Lock.
